categories.main_business_segments: Kyoei Steel operates three main business segments: Domestic Steel Business (manufacturing and sales of steel products for civil engineering and construction in Japan), Overseas Steel Business (manufacturing and sales of steel products in Vietnam, the US, and Canada), and Environmental Recycling Business (intermediate and final treatment of medical and industrial waste, and recycled crushed stone). The company also engages in ancillary businesses such as port operations, casting, and insurance agency services.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core technology is electric arc furnace (EAF) steelmaking, which melts steel scrap to produce steel products in a resource-circulating model. It has developed proprietary processes for high-strength rebar, screw-threaded rebar (Tough Neji Bar®), and integrated steelmaking and rolling lines. In environmental recycling, it utilizes high-temperature EAFs for the safe melting and detoxification of medical and industrial waste, and operates gasification melting furnaces for industrial waste.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Kyoei Steel primarily serves the construction and civil engineering sectors, supplying rebar and structural steel to construction companies, general contractors, and steel distributors. Its main end markets are public and private infrastructure, building construction, and, in the overseas segment, also mining (grinding media). Major customers include trading houses such as Hanwa Co., Ltd.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates in Japan (with four main domestic plants), Vietnam (multiple steel plants and a port), the United States (Texas), and Canada (Alberta). Sales are split between Japan and overseas, with significant operations and investments in Vietnam and North America, aiming for a 'three-pillar' global structure.
categories.supply_chain_position: Kyoei Steel is a midstream and downstream player in the steel supply chain. It procures steel scrap (upstream), processes it into steel products (midstream), and supplies finished and semi-finished products to construction and industrial customers (downstream). In recycling, it also handles upstream waste collection and midstream processing.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include strengthening the North American business, restructuring and improving profitability in Vietnam, and enhancing the domestic four-plant system. The company is investing in smart factories, digital transformation (DX), and ESG initiatives, with a strong focus on decarbonization (50% CO2 reduction by 2030), circular economy, and high-value-added product development. R&D targets high-strength and differentiated steel products, new construction methods, and advanced recycling technologies.
categories.revenue_model: Kyoei Steel generates revenue primarily through the sale of steel products (rebar, structural steel, billets, processed steel), waste treatment services (medical and industrial), and ancillary services such as port operations and casting. Revenue is recognized at the point of delivery for steel products and upon completion of waste treatment services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Major competitors include other Japanese electric arc furnace steelmakers and global rebar producers. In Japan, it holds a top share in the rebar market. Overseas, it competes with local and regional steelmakers in Vietnam and North America. The company positions itself as a cost-competitive, resource-circulating steelmaker with a unique integrated recycling business.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated sales were ¥322.8 billion, with operating profit of ¥15.3 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders of ¥10.8 billion. The company has around 3,900 employees. While domestic sales have been stable, overseas operations, especially in Vietnam, have faced challenges, but the company is investing for growth in North America and aims for ¥380 billion in sales and ¥25 billion in recurring profit by FY2026.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Kyoei Steel differentiates itself through its resource-circulating business model, combining steelmaking with advanced waste recycling, and its commitment to sustainability (e.g., 'Ethical Steel' branding). It emphasizes cost competitiveness, stable supply, and the ability to offer traceable, low-carbon steel products. Its unique integration of steel production and environmental solutions addresses both customer needs and societal challenges.
